environmental.operating-temp: to 70 C - 325 A per panel at 45 C, de-rated to 200 A at 70 C; no lower limit is stated

management.alarm-contacts: Form C relay per side, 2 A at 30 VDC and 0.6 A at 60 VDC, on wire-wrap terminals

physical.overall-mm: 431.8 x 44 x 478 without tie bar, 559 deep with the tie bar it ships with (17 x 1.75 x 18.8 in)
physical.weight-configured-scope: populated, 19.6 lb in the datasheet; unpopulated is 14.6 lb

power.input-dc: dual feed; maximum input load 325 A at 45 C per panel, de-rated to 200 A at 70 C; input wire 2/0 AWG to 350 MCM; output wire #14 to #6 AWG in P40 connectors
power.output-breaker-max: 60 A single-pole; the UL rating holds to 48 A continuous per output
power.power-max-scope: the alarm card alone at 48 V (30 mA); 0.48 W at 24 V and 0.22 W at 12 V. It is the only thing in the panel that draws. Separately the guide gives a nominal power LOSS of less than 45 W per side at 325 A and 48 V, which is heat in the conductors and not a draw.

configs.description: The panel as it ships: no breakers, a blanking cover over every position, and no output plugs. Breakers and connector kits are sold separately.

configs.description: Side A on breakers and side B on TPA fuses in their holders, to show the two things a position takes. An illustration; the vendor sells the holder and the fuses for this panel and publishes no standard fill.

breaker-ratings.note: ONE MODULE CARRIES ELEVEN RATINGS AS A FIELD. The datasheet sells breakers from 2 A to 60 A as eleven part numbers that differ in nothing but the figure printed on the handle, so they are one part with a `rating` field, set per position in a configuration. Each breaker ships with a touch guard seated on it, a separate part that a configuration can take off. The populated example is an invented load to show the field working; the vendor publishes no standard fill.

chassis.note: 431.8 wide and 43.9 high as the 300CB08. THE CHASSIS IS 367.0 DEEP, front of the metal to the tops of the output receptacles, READ OFF THE -C BOTTOM VIEW, Fig. 3-13 (upper), at 1.493 px/mm on both axes: the drawing prints 462.2 from the front of the metal to the tip of the longer busbar landing, 543.6 with the tie bar and 558.4 overall, and all three agree with its 644 px across the 431.8 body to a tenth. The receptacle tops lie 367.4 from the front on it, and 366.4 on the nrgILS300CB08-C bottom view beside it (p43, 1.190 px/mm). THIS IS 36.2 MORE THAN THE 300CB08's 330.8: the bottom pan of a -C panel runs about 335, where the stud panel's is shorter, so the -C is not the stud chassis with busbars added (#860). The busbars stand behind that, on the input parts. The datasheet gives 478 without the tie bar, which is the 462.2 plus the 14.7 the front guards stand proud.

ears.note: NOT DRAWN. The panel ships with separate 19 inch and 23 inch mounting brackets (PMTG19, PMTG23) that bolt to the sides; Fig. 3-1 dimensions them at 482.6 and 584.2 over the body.

envelope-faces.note: Top, bottom, left and right are sized from the 367.0 chassis. THE BOTTOM IS READ off this version's own bottom view, Fig. 3-13 (upper), at 1.493 px/mm, origin the receptacle tops: the rear pair of vent fields 144.0 deep from 33.1, the front pair 86.4 deep from 246.0, and the two ground bolts at 216.0 across, drawn on the stated 5/8 inch centres, one pair (see ground-pairs), its screws 15.875 apart about 49.0. The top is given the two side fields the photographs show running the depth of the lid, their extent estimated. THE SIDES ARE THE STUD PANEL'S SIDE VIEW, Fig. 3-4 at 1.717 px/mm, not re-read for this version (gap c-side-view): four bracket holes 29.1 apart starting 11.1 from the front, placed from the front, and a two-bolt ground landing on 5/8 inch centres placed from the REAR, 62 from it as on the stud panel and so 305.0 from the front here; the side lug Fig. 3-13 draws lies about 65 from the rear. Each side carries one landing and the bottom a third; the guide says only one ground connection is required.

front.note: Breaker cells, thumbscrews, lamp holes, switch slots and the designation card slot are measured on Fig. 3-1. Sixteen cells 17.8 x 39.1 on a 19.81 pitch (39 px), the first at 14.2 and the ninth at 261.1, which mirror about the centre to a tenth. What is printed on the front comes from the front photograph in the same guide (Fig. 1-1) and its positions are fractions of the centre panel read off that photograph, which is taken from slightly above: the wording is as printed, the positions are approximate. The DC, alarm and electrostatic symbols are drawn as plain strokes in the places the photograph shows them; their exact artwork is not resolved at that size. The front prints in dark ink on the pale panel.

front-cover.note: THE FRONT FACE IS A REMOVABLE COVER. The guide has a procedure for it (section 2.2.7): two thumbscrews release a bar that spans the front, with sixteen openings the breaker guards show through and the lamps, switch slots and card slot in its centre. It is drawn as the panel, not as a part, because the panel is never seen without it in service and the breakers, not the cover, are what a position holds. The slot under the lamps is the designation card holder the datasheet lists.

ground-pairs.note: EACH LANDING IS ONE PAIR, NOT TWO STUDS (#828, #830). The installation guide's three sets of 1/4-20 threaded holes on 5/8 inch centres are each the landing of one dual-hole lug, so each is common/ground-stud-pair-5-8-1-4@1, two 1/4-20 pan-head screws at exactly 15.875, the pitch of the stud-pair-5-8 interface (formerly two common/ground-stud@1 placements 15.9 apart). Each pair is placed at rotate 90, one screw above the other as the side view, Fig. 3-4, and the bottom view draw the landings, centred where the two studs' midpoint was. A two-hole lug seated on a pair leaves its wire down the face (toward the front on the bottom view); each screw still takes a single-hole lug on its own, which the guide also allows. The earth mark beside each side landing is centred on its pair, 1.8 lower than it sat beside the two studs.

ground-stud-size.note: The installation guide is one document for every version of the panel and its grounding specification is not limited to a version, as its input rows are: three sets of 1/4-20 threaded holes on 5/8 inch centres, bolted with washers to 50 in-lb, for a dual-hole compression lug on #6 to #1 AWG wire. Its description says the ground terminals take either a dual-hole or a single-hole lug and that only one ground connection is required. That is the `stud-size` of all three ground pairs, one on each side and one on the bottom.

lamps.note: Fig. 3-1 draws five lamp holes on a 12.7 pitch. Fig. 2-11 names them for the monitored panel as A PWR, A ALM, nrg, B ALM, B PWR, and section 1.4 says the alarm card controls four indicator LEDs on the front. So the plain panel has four lamps in the outer four holes and the centre hole, the nrg position, is not lit. The guide gives the colours in its power-up steps (section 2.2.9): a PWR lamp is green when its feed is present, and an ALM lamp is red when a breaker on that side is off or tripped with its alarm switch enabled. The front photograph shows something in the centre hole too; what fills it is not established.

lifecycle.note: searched 2026-10-05 for an end-of-life, end-of-sale or discontinuation notice for the 300CB08 and found none; the vendor product page lists it as current. The installation guide marks a different part, the original nrg300CB08, as EOL and replaced by the -SENS and -CTRL versions.

method.note: THE FRONT, TOP AND SIDES ARE THE 300CB08's, and are taken from it: the guide draws one front view for every passive version (Fig. 3-1), and this file repeats the readings amphenol-ns/300cb08 made of it. What is particular to this version is the rear, read from its own figure in section 3 of the installation guide, and its weight, from the datasheet. THE BOTTOM AND THE DEPTH ARE THIS VERSION'S OWN, read off its bottom view, Fig. 3-13 (upper) (provenance.chassis, provenance.envelope-faces). NOT READ: the side view the guide gives for this version; its bracket holes and ground landing are the plain panel's, placed from the front and the rear of the deeper chassis.

ratings.note: The datasheet gives the maximum input load as 325A @ 45 C per panel. The installation guide prints the same row with its de-rating: 325A @45 C per panel (De-rated to 200A @70 C). That is the only temperature either document states for the panel, so it is what `operating-temp` carries: a ceiling with its two rating points, and no lower limit.

rear.note: Fig. 3-8, the embedded 1399 x 199 image on page 40, at 2.849 px/mm, scaled on the body between its two edges (85 to 1315 px) taken as 431.8, which then reads 43.9 high. Sixteen P40 receptacles on a 13.41 pitch, as on the -SC. Each input is two horizontal busbar landings seen end-on, and the drawing prints what the stud versions do not: a large B at the left end and A at the right, and BATTERY and RETURN beside each assembly, BATTERY on the OUTER side of both. SIDE A IS THE MIRROR OF SIDE B: the narrow landing, 6.0 against 7.7, is the outer one on each (26.3 and 399.8 from the left), so the side A feed is the same part turned 180 degrees and its `landing-1` is BATTERY on both sides.

rear-cover.note: NOT DRAWN. A clear polycarbonate cover closes the whole rear over the input and output terminals (datasheet, Primary Features; guide Fig. 2-20). It is transparent and everything behind it is what the rear view shows.

tie-bar.note: NOT DRAWN. The panel ships with a rear tie bar for dressing the output cables (guide Fig. 2-2 and 2-25), and takes an optional four-post bracket kit, 307622. Cable management is not drawn; the datasheet depth with the bar fitted is recorded.
